title: Eggs Benedict
subtitle: Poached eggs with grilled pancetta and hollandaise
excerpt: Eggs Benedict combines perfectly poached eggs with crispy grilled pancetta and a rich butter hollandaise. The hollandaise is the hardest part and needs full attention. Take it slowly and it will come together.
sourceNotes: Eggs Benedict is thought to have originated in New York in the late 1800s. The British version often uses back bacon or grilled pancetta in place of Canadian ham.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Clarify the butter up to 3 days ahead. Keep warm or gently re-melt before making the sauce.

content.text: Make the hollandaise last and keep it warm over a very low heat. Poach the eggs just before serving. Everything else can wait.
Clarify the butter: melt it gently in a small pan. Skim off the white foam. Pour the clear yellow butter into a jug, leaving the milky solids behind.
Set a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water. The bowl must not touch the water.
Put the egg yolks, a splash of water, and the mustard in the bowl. Whisk constantly for 3 to 4 minutes until pale and thick.
Remove the bowl from the heat. Pour in the warm clarified butter very slowly, whisking all the time. Start with drops, then a thin trickle.
When all the butter is in, add the lemon juice and season with salt. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.
Keep the hollandaise warm over the hot water with the heat off. Stir now and then.
Grill the pancetta in a dry frying pan until crisp. Set aside.
Fill the large saucepan with water to a depth of about 6 cm. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Crack one egg into a small cup. Stir the water to create a gentle swirl, then slide the egg in. Repeat with up to 3 more eggs.
Poach for 3 minutes for a runny yolk. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
To serve: place pancetta on a plate, top with a poached egg, and spoon hollandaise generously over the top.

items.symptom: The hollandaise has split and looks greasy or curdled.
items.cause: Butter was added too fast or the mixture got too hot.
items.fix: Whisk a fresh yolk in a clean bowl, then slowly whisk in the split sauce.

items.symptom: The poached eggs are spreading into wispy strands.
items.cause: Eggs are not fresh enough or the water is boiling too hard.
items.fix: Use the freshest eggs and keep water at a gentle simmer only.

items.symptom: The hollandaise is too thick to pour.
items.cause: It cooled too much or reduced slightly.
items.fix: Whisk in a teaspoon of warm water to loosen it.
